verdict: Cummins grew revenue 13% to $9.4B and posted record profit margins, powered by data-center demand for its power-generation equipment — net income more than doubled to $1.14B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $3.86 a year ago; includes a $0.54 favorable tax item

segments.name: Engine
segments.note: Engines for trucks and construction equipment — external sales of $2,389M (total segment sales $3,130M including $741M sold to other Cummins segments). North America revenue rose 21% on stronger truck demand.

segments.name: Components
segments.note: Turbochargers, filters, transmissions and other parts — external sales of $2,397M (total $2,856M). US truck demand drove North America up 35%.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.note: Selling, servicing and supporting Cummins products worldwide — the largest slice of external sales, lifted by power-generation demand, especially for data centers.

segments.name: Power Systems
segments.note: Generators and power systems — external sales of $1,250M (total $2,289M including $1,039M of intersegment sales). The profit star: 25.4% EBITDA margin on data-center demand.

segments.name: Accelera
segments.note: The zero-emissions unit — batteries, hydrogen and electric powertrains. External sales fell to $95M as electrolyzer sales dropped after a strategic review; it lost $56M of EBITDA.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company.

opex.name: Research, development & engineering
opex.note: Developing engines and power systems, including the upcoming HELM engine platforms.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: Miscellaneous operating costs — far below the $247M a year ago, which included Accelera charges.

opex.name: Equity, royalty & interest income from investees
opex.note: Income, not a cost: earnings from businesses Cummins part-owns, plus royalty and interest income from them — it offsets operating costs on the way to operating income.

otherDetail: A net $24M cost below operating profit: $57M of other income, outweighed by $81M of interest expense.
footerNote: Segment figures are external sales (what each segment sold to outside customers); total segment sales including sales between Cummins segments were Engine $3,130M, Components $2,856M, Distribution $3,310M, Power Systems $2,289M and Accelera $103M. The flow uses consolidated net income of $1,169M; after $29M attributable to noncontrolling interests, net income attributable to Cummins was $1,140M ($8.25 per diluted share). Segment YoY is computed from external sales a year ago.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Data centers need power — Cummins sells it
takeaways.text: Power Systems earned a 25.4% EBITDA margin on $2.3B of total sales, up 15%. Demand for power generation, especially for data centers in the US, China and Asia Pacific, is the strongest thread in the whole quarter.

takeaways.title: A record quarter, with a tax assist
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS more than doubled to $8.25 — helped by $0.54 a share of favorable one-off tax items, and by comparison with a year-ago quarter that carried $240M ($1.73 a share) of Accelera write-down charges.

takeaways.title: Cash went back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Cummins returned $661M in dividends and buybacks in the quarter and still expects about 10% revenue growth for the full year, with EBITDA margins around 18.2%.

oneTimers: Diluted EPS includes $0.54 per share of favorable discrete tax items — one-off tax benefits that will not necessarily repeat.
The year-ago quarter included $240M ($1.73 per diluted share) of non-cash Accelera charges, which is why this quarter's profit growth looks so large.
